q: Chromium has the electronic configuration $[Ar] 4s^1 3d^5$ instead of $[Ar] 4s^2 3d^4$ because _____ 3d orbitals have extra stability.
e: Half-filled 3d orbitals provide extra stability, causing the 4s electron to shift.

q: Copper has the electronic configuration $[Ar] 4s^1 3d^{10}$ because _____ 3d orbitals have extra stability.
e: Completely filled 3d orbitals provide extra stability for copper.

q: When transition metals form ions, the electrons are always removed first from the _____ orbital and then from the 3d orbitals.
e: Electrons are removed from the outermost 4s orbital before the 3d orbitals.

q: The electronic configuration of the iron(II) ion ($Fe^{2+}$) is _____.
e: Fe loses two 4s electrons to form $Fe^{2+}$, leaving $[Ar] 3d^6$.

q: The electronic configuration of the iron(III) ion ($Fe^{3+}$) is _____.
e: Fe loses two 4s and one 3d electron to form $Fe^{3+}$, leaving $[Ar] 3d^5$.

q: The zinc element always loses the 2 outer electrons from 4s to give the electronic configuration of _____ when it forms an ion.
e: Zinc loses its two 4s electrons to form $Zn^{2+}$ with a stable $[Ar] 3d^{10}$ configuration.

q: Copper is considered a transition element because the $Cu^{2+}$ ion has _____ 3d orbitals.
e: The $Cu^{2+}$ ion has an incomplete 3d subshell ($[Ar] 3d^9$), satisfying the IUPAC definition.

q: The electronic configuration of the $Cu^{2+}$ ion is _____.
e: Cu loses one 4s and one 3d electron to form $Cu^{2+}$ ($[Ar] 3d^9$).

q: In a transition series, the properties of transition elements are very similar because the valence shell electron configuration of the elements _____.
e: Properties are similar because the valence shell electron configuration remains effectively unchanged.

q: Most of the first series of transition elements are more important and technically important than the _____ members of their groups.
e: The 3d series elements are generally more technically important than heavier members.

q: The transition elements are solid metals and are silvery-white except for copper, which is _____ in colour.
e: Copper is distinctively brownish-red in colour.

q: Gold is used in jewellery because of its beautiful yellow lustre colour and its inertness to oxygen and _____.
e: Gold is inert to both oxygen and water.

q: One cubic centimetre ($1 cm^3$) cube of iron is _____ times heavier than a $1 cm^3$ cube of sodium.
e: Transition metals have high density; iron is 8 times heavier than sodium for the same volume.

q: Transition elements are significantly _____ reactive than Group I metals.
e: Transition elements are much less reactive than alkali metals.

q: In general, transition metals do not corrode readily in the atmosphere, but _____ is an exception because it rusts easily.
e: Iron is a notable exception as it rusts easily in the atmosphere.

q: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called _____.
e: Iron and carbon combine to form the alloy steel.

q: Most transition elements form coloured compounds, in contrast to Groups 1 and 2 metals which form _____ compounds.
e: Groups 1 and 2 metals typically form white or colourless compounds.

q: The transition elements show variable oxidation states and can form more than one compound with another element, such as copper(I) oxide and _____.
e: Copper forms both copper(I) oxide ($Cu_2O$) and copper(II) oxide ($CuO$).

q: Most transition elements can form complex ions, which is an ion that has a _____ at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions surrounding it.
e: A complex ion features a central metal ion surrounded by ligands.

q: The +3 oxidation states are more stable at the beginning of the series, i.e., the left side of Mn, whereas towards the end, _____ oxidation states are more stable.
e: Towards the right side of Mn, the +2 oxidation state becomes more stable.

q: The elements in the _____ of the series exhibit more oxidation states than those to the left or right.
e: Elements in the middle of the 3d series exhibit the widest range of oxidation states.

q: Iron is known to form oxidation states from +2 to +6, with iron(II) and _____ being the most common.
e: Iron(II) and iron(III) are the most common and stable oxidation states for iron.

q: The highest oxidation state is _____ for manganese.
e: Manganese exhibits a maximum oxidation state of +7.

q: The ions of chromium, manganese, and iron have the highest oxidation states +6, +7, and +6 respectively, and these ions tend to be good _____ agents.
e: Ions in their highest oxidation states act as strong oxidising agents.

q: Vanadium and chromium ions with the lowest oxidation state of +2 are good _____ agents.
e: Ions in their lowest oxidation states act as good reducing agents.

q: Because of their greater nuclear attraction force, divalent ions of $Co^{2+}$, $Ni^{2+}$, $Cu^{2+}$, and $Zn^{2+}$ are poor _____ agents.
e: These divalent ions are poor reducing agents due to greater nuclear attraction.

q: Transition metals usually have their highest oxidation states in compounds with high electronegative elements such as oxygen and _____.
e: Highest oxidation states are typically found in compounds with oxygen and fluorine.

q: Examples of highest oxidation states include vanadium(V) fluoride ($VF_5$), chromium(VI) oxide ($CrO_3$), and manganese(VII) oxide (_____).
e: Manganese(VII) oxide has the formula $Mn_2O_7$.

q: The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of incomplete d orbitals or the presence of _____ electrons.
e: Unpaired d electrons are responsible for the absorption of visible light and colour.

q: The transition metal compounds form coloured ions in an aqueous solution because they absorb part of the visible light and transmit the _____ colour.
e: The transmitted colour is the complement of the absorbed wavelength.

q: The $Sc^{3+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$ ions are colourless because $Sc^{3+}$ ion has completely empty d orbitals, and $Zn^{2+}$ has _____ d orbitals.
e: $Zn^{2+}$ has completely filled 3d orbitals, preventing d-d transitions.

q: According to the colours of 3d series transition metal ions in aqueous solutions, the $Ti^{3+}$ ion is _____ in colour.
e: The $Ti^{3+}$ ion appears purple in aqueous solution.

q: The $V^{3+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $V^{3+}$ ion is green in aqueous solution.

q: The $Cr^{3+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Cr^{3+}$ ion appears violet in aqueous solution.

q: The $Mn^{2+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Mn^{2+}$ ion is pale pink in aqueous solution.

q: The $Fe^{2+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Fe^{2+}$ ion appears green in aqueous solution.

q: The $Fe^{3+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Fe^{3+}$ ion is yellow in aqueous solution.

q: The $Co^{2+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Co^{2+}$ ion appears pink in aqueous solution.

q: The $Ni^{2+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Ni^{2+}$ ion is green in aqueous solution.

q: The $Cu^{2+}$ ion is _____ in colour in an aqueous solution.
e: The $Cu^{2+}$ ion is distinctly blue in aqueous solution.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are unpaired then the transition metal is a _____ substance.
e: Substances with unpaired electrons are paramagnetic.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are paired, then the transition metal is a _____ substance.
e: Substances with all paired electrons are diamagnetic.

q: Substances that are attracted very strongly by the applied magnetic field and retain magnetisation are said to be _____.
e: Ferromagnetic substances are strongly attracted and retain magnetisation.

q: According to electronic configurations, scandium, titanium, vanadium, chromium, and manganese are _____ substances.
e: These elements have unpaired d electrons, making them paramagnetic.

q: According to the textbook, copper and zinc are _____ substances.
e: The text explicitly classifies copper and zinc as diamagnetic substances.

q: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are _____ substances.
e: Fe, Co, and Ni are strongly magnetic and classified as ferromagnetic.

q: Iron is used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia in the _____ process.
e: The Haber process uses iron as a catalyst to synthesize ammonia.

q: Vanadium is used in the form of vanadium(V) oxide as a catalyst in the manufacture of sulphuric acid in the _____ process.
e: The Contact process uses $V_2O_5$ to produce sulphuric acid.

q: Nickel is used as a catalyst in the _____ of alkenes.
e: Nickel catalyzes the hydrogenation of alkenes.

q: Titanium(IV) chloride ($TiCl_4$) is used for the manufacturing of _____ in industries.
e: $TiCl_4$ is a catalyst for manufacturing high-density polyethene.

q: Titanium is an integral part of modern construction because it is highly corrosion-resistant, strong, and _____.
e: Titanium's combination of strength and lightweight nature makes it ideal for construction.

q: Iron is usually mixed with small amounts of other elements to make harder _____ with greater tensile strength.
e: Iron is alloyed to form harder alloy steels.

q: Manganese steel is extremely strong and is used for _____.
e: The extreme strength of manganese steel makes it suitable for railway tracks.

q: Vanadium(V) oxide ($V_2O_5$) is used as a catalyst in the _____ industry and as a mordant in the printing and dyeing of fabrics.
e: $V_2O_5$ finds use as a catalyst in the ceramics industry.

q: Chromium is widely used for manufacturing _____.
e: Chromium is a key component in manufacturing stainless steel.

q: In the automobile industry, chromium is involved in the production of car _____.
e: Chromium is used in the production of car brake pads.

q: Manganese is used as a catalyst to reduce the _____ rating in gasoline.
e: Manganese acts as a catalyst related to the octane rating in gasoline.

q: Cobalt ion has a brilliant _____ colour used as paint, ink, and pigments.
e: Cobalt ions produce a brilliant blue colour.

q: Nickel is primarily used in the production of _____.
e: A primary industrial use of nickel is in stainless steel production.

q: Copper is a good conductor of electricity and it is used for electrical wire, circuit boards, and _____.
e: Copper's durability and conductivity make it suitable for water pipes.

q: Iron is used in modern medicine to treat and prevent _____.
e: Iron supplements are used to treat and prevent anemia.

q: Copper has been used in medicine to treat Wilson's disease and _____ disease.
e: Copper is used to treat both Wilson's and Menkes diseases.

q: Titanium surgical instruments offer advantages over stainless steel instruments, such as being lightweight, durable, and _____.
e: Titanium is highly corrosion-resistant, making it ideal for surgical tools.

q: Titanium has been used mostly for fabricating _____.
e: Titanium is widely used for fabricating dental implants.

q: Nichrome wire is an alloy used in electric _____.
e: Nichrome wire is commonly used in electric stoves.

q: Titanium is also used for _____, ships, and marine equipment.
e: Titanium's properties make it valuable for spacecraft construction.

q: In the chemical industry, vanadium metal _____ are widely used.
e: Vanadium metal sheets, wires, and tubes are widely used in the chemical industry.

q: Chromium is mainly used in _____, tanning, printing, dyeing, catalysts, oxidants, matches, and metal corrosion inhibitors.
e: Electroplating is a major industrial application for chromium.

q: Manganese is also used in _____, and paint.
e: Manganese is a key component in dry cell batteries.

q: Nickel is used for _____, and nickel plating.
e: Nickel provides effective anti-corrosion coatings.

q: It is also used in _____ replacements, and eyeglass frames.
e: Titanium is used in artificial hip bone replacements.

q: Vanadium compounds are also used as a _____ in the printing and dyeing of fabrics.
e: Vanadium compounds act as a mordant in fabric dyeing.

q: Vanadium is used to form alloys of steel with _____.
e: Vanadium forms alloys of steel primarily with iron.

q: Various chromium salts are the main raw materials in the _____ industry.
e: Chromium salts are fundamental raw materials in the chemical industry.

q: Cobalt is primarily used in the ceramics and paint industry to create the _____ colour.
e: Cobalt is famous for producing a brilliant blue colour in paints and ceramics.
